Package io.github.jspinak.brobot.action.basic.find.motion

Class FindMotion

java.lang.Object
io.github.jspinak.brobot.action.basic.find.motion.FindMotion
@Component public class FindMotion extends Object
Detects and tracks motion across multiple scene captures. This class implements motion detection by analyzing changes between three consecutive screenshots to identify moving objects and distinguish them from the background.

The motion detection algorithm requires three scenes:

  • Scene 1 and 2: Used to detect initial motion
  • Scene 2 and 3: Used to confirm motion and track trajectory
  • All 3 scenes: Used to distinguish moving objects from background changes

Key features:

  • Identifies moving objects by tracking similar trajectories across scenes
  • Filters out background changes that appear stationary
  • Supports configurable time intervals between captures
  • Provides visual illustrations of detected motion

The TimeBetweenIndividualActions option in ActionConfig controls the time interval (in seconds) between screenshot captures.

  • Method Details

    • find

      public void find(ActionResult matches, List<ObjectCollection> objectCollections)
      Finds motion by analyzing changes across three consecutive scene captures. This method implements a sophisticated motion detection algorithm that distinguishes moving objects from background changes by tracking consistent trajectories.

      The algorithm works as follows:

      • Captures 3 scenes at specified time intervals
      • Detects changes between scenes 1-2 and scenes 2-3
      • Identifies objects with consistent motion trajectories
      • Filters out stationary background changes

      When images are provided in objectCollections, they can be used to track specific objects. Without provided images, all detected motion is returned. For screen motion detection, use empty or no ObjectCollection.

      Side effects:

      • Populates matches with detected moving objects
      • Sets scene analysis collection in matches
      • Creates motion illustrations for each scene
      • Sorts matches by score in descending order
      Parameters:
      matches - the ActionResult to populate with motion matches
      objectCollections - collections containing images to analyze (can be empty for screen capture)

    • getRegionsOfChange

      public List<Match> getRegionsOfChange(SceneAnalyses sceneAnalysisCollection, int index1, int index2, MotionFindOptions actionConfig, List<Region> searchRegions)
      Detects regions of change between two scenes and returns them as matches. This method uses absolute difference to identify changed pixels, then finds contours around these regions to create match objects.

      The process involves:

      • Computing absolute difference between two scenes
      • Finding contours in the difference image
      • Filtering contours by area and search region constraints
      • Creating match objects for valid motion regions

      Side effects:

      • Sets contours in the scene analysis collection
      • Creates motion illustrations for the second scene
      Parameters:
      sceneAnalysisCollection - collection containing scenes to analyze
      index1 - index of the first scene in the collection
      index2 - index of the second scene in the collection
      actionConfig - provides min/max area constraints for valid contours
      searchRegions - list of regions to limit motion detection (empty = full scene)
      Returns:
      list of Match objects representing detected motion regions
      See Also:
      • ContourExtractor
      • MotionDetector.getDynamicPixelMask(org.bytedeco.opencv.opencv_core.Mat, org.bytedeco.opencv.opencv_core.Mat)
